notes: 5 of the first 5 rows are one player's own deck (players 1): they describe that player, not what this population plays. Pass min_players 2 (or sort players) for decks played across players.

1152 battles in this window are outside the meta population and not counted anywhere above (excluded.outside_meta): event battles and decks the player did not choose (6.17.0). battles_query and battles_decks read them.

These are the population's decks and levels; nothing here checks what a given player holds. Before naming a row as a recommendation to a person, pass fit_for with their tag: rows they cannot field leave decks[], and every row then says what they would field it at and what upgrades would open.

archetype is Elixir's descriptive name for a deck's shape - its win condition and family, composed from the cards and their costs - not a claim about what players call it or how it performs; several deck identities (forms) share one label, and a deck with no attested win condition is named by its cost alone.

Win rates here are NOT comparable across rows: deck 8a7dc50e… was played 100% in ranked (mean level gap -0.04) and deck 7f857c21… 96% in ladder (gap +0.03); matchmaking differs by mode (war draws opponents from the racing clans, not from your trophies, so a strong player meets weaker ones there) and a level gap moves the expected win rate, so rank decks only within one mode and similar mean_level_gap (pass mode; the record describes the gap and does not adjust for it).
Pooled across modes: ladder 791 (mean level gap +0.17), ranked 712 (mean level gap +0.03), war 193 (mean level gap +0.12), casual 64 (mean level gap +0.00); pass mode to isolate one.
Every deck row here was played by ONE player (players: 1): this segment's numbers describe a few players' habits, not a meta; widen the segment or read the corpus for the field.
Pooled player-battle observations, not unique matches: both participants can contribute, so counts are dependent.
Only decided head-to-head battles count; `excluded` says how many duels, boat battles, draws and unresolved outcomes the window held.

shrunk_win_rate shrinks toward the CORPUS mean over the same window and mode, and is withheld (null, insufficient_sample: true) when the population is under 30 decided observations, not per row: a row with few battles still carries one, shrunk hard toward the mean. win_rate is the raw rate at any sample size, so read it beside battles.
Shrinkage moderates extremes but does not adjust for skill or guarantee rank order; no confidence intervals.
